about: slapstic page 0 $85EC-$8BFF: the AT-AT walkers of the walker part - set-up of the three records at atat_rec, their per-frame movement (spawning, head swing, walking, falling, the legs bonus) and their view (body, legs, head, the head's aim at the player)

P0:85EC.name: atat_init
P0:85EC.desc: set-up of the AT-ATs for the walker part, called by wave2_setup: loads the points of objects $17 and $18 into the math box, clears atat_under and fills the three $19-byte records at atat_rec from atat_init_tab with their type byte left 0 (free), then sets w2_spawn_b to 3 so that atat_move_all brings them in one at a time

P0:8674.name: atat_demo_init
P0:8674.desc: set-up of the demo AT-AT of the training manual, called by man_init_walker and man_show_atat with B = the manual page: fills the first record from entry B of atat_demo_tab (entry 0 when B is over 2) as a standing walker, frees the other two records, loads the points of objects $17 and $18 and clears w2_spawn_b so that nothing is spawned

P0:8705.name: atat_move_all
P0:8705.desc: per-frame movement of the AT-ATs, called by the walker phases and by man_move_walker. while w2_spawn_b is positive it respawns one free record (P0_9163), when it is negative (end of the part) it frees the walkers that are neither falling nor in view nor over the player, then it awards the legs bonus when the player comes under a walker (atat_under remembers which one until the player has left it), and for every live record counts it in w2_active_b, runs down its shot delay, swings the head, moves it by its mode and steps the walk cycle. a falling walker carries the height of the tow cable's end down with it

P0:8828.name: atat_head_swing
P0:8828.desc: moves the head of the AT-AT record at U: adds the pitch rate to the pitch angle and the yaw rate to the yaw angle, turning a rate round at random when the angle would leave its range, and takes the size of each rate (1 to 3) from a table indexed by the angle. when the head saw the player in the last view but was not yet aimed, the two rates are first pointed towards the player by the signs atat_head_aim left in bytes $17 and $18

P0:88DE.name: atat_move_mode
P0:88DE.desc: calls the movement routine for the mode in byte 4 of the AT-AT record at U through atat_move_tab: 0 stand, 1 walk, 2 fall (a mode over 2 counts as 0)

P0:88F0.name: atat_mode_stand
P0:88F0.desc: movement mode 0 of an AT-AT, standing: does nothing. reached through atat_move_tab, hence no caller found

P0:88F1.name: atat_mode_walk
P0:88F1.desc: movement mode 1 of an AT-AT, walking: adds $33 to the x position of the record at U. reached through atat_move_tab, hence no caller found

P0:88F9.name: atat_mode_fall
P0:88F9.desc: movement mode 2 of an AT-AT, falling after the tow cable caught its legs: lowers the height of the record at U by $0400 a frame and, when it reaches the ground, calls P0_9006 which blows the walker up, scores it and respawns it. reached through atat_move_tab, hence no caller found

P0:8912.name: atat_step_anim
P0:8912.desc: adds 1 to the walk cycle counter in byte $15 of the AT-AT record at U, the time the leg drawing (P0_8C27) follows the leg tracks with

P0:891A.name: atat_view_all
P0:891A.desc: view of the AT-ATs, called by vew_walker, by the game over view and by man_view_walker with Y at the display list. for every live record it clears the frame's flags in byte 1 (the hit flash is kept only while the walker was drawn last frame), writes the colour (green, or the flash list when hit), sets the ship 2 block to a unit matrix and concatenates it, crashes the ship (P0_913C) when it is under a falling walker, and draws the body, the legs and the head

P0:898C.name: atat_view_body
P0:898C.desc: views the centre of the AT-AT at U from the ship (pre-subtract MS_PSB2 on its position), keeps the result in M_XT, M_YT and M_ZT for the legs and the head, and calls atat_draw_body when the centre is ahead between $0010 and $4000 and within 45 degrees of the line of sight both ways

P0:89E4.name: atat_draw_body
P0:89E4.desc: draws the body of the AT-AT at U, object $17: marks the record drawn and its body in view (bits $10 and $40 of byte 1), dims the colour with the distance beyond $2000, has bank 1 view and draw the object's points and tests the lazar against the body (P0_8EE1)

P0:8A1C.name: atat_view_legs
P0:8A1C.desc: draws the four legs of the AT-AT at U: only a call of P0_8C27

P0:8A20.name: atat_view_head
P0:8A20.desc: views the head of the AT-AT at U: post-adds the head's offset in bytes 11 to 16 of the record to the viewed centre and, when that point is ahead between $0010 and $4000 and within 45 degrees both ways, sets the colour (dimmed beyond $2000, else full brightness unless the hit flash is on), makes the point the new M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT and calls atat_draw_head

P0:8AA5.name: atat_head_aim
P0:8AA5.desc: aim of the head's guns at the player, called while the head is drawn with U at the AT-AT record. only when the head faces the ship: finds the muzzle of the gun on the side given by bit 7 of the type byte, moves the ship 2 block there and views the player from it. with the player in front the head turns red, bit 2 of byte 1 is set and the player's side and height are left in bytes $17 and $18 for atat_head_swing. with the player within 45 degrees (always from w2_level_b 9 up) the head flashes, bit 1 is set and, when the record may shoot and its delay has run out, a shot is started on page 1 (P1_8F8B) and the gun side changed. ends with the lazar test on the guns (P0_8FA6)

P0:8B82.name: atat_draw_head
P0:8B82.desc: draws the head of the AT-AT at U: marks the record drawn, yaws and pitches the ship 2 block by a quarter of the head's two angles and concatenates it, views the points of object $18 and draws object $1A (only when the body is in view), object $18 and, after the lazar test on the head (P0_8F64) and atat_head_aim, object $19

4C3D.name: atat_col_ptr
4C3D.desc: word: display list address of the colour instruction atat_view_all wrote for the AT-AT being viewed. P0_913C overwrites that instruction with the flash list call when the ship runs into the walker

4C3F.name: atat_under
4C3F.desc: word: address of the AT-AT record the player is flying under, 0 when none. set by atat_move_all when the player comes within $07D0 by $03E8 of a walker and the legs bonus is scored, cleared when the player is $0BB8 by $05DC away or the walker is gone, so one pass scores once

4AD2.name: cable_rec
4AD2.desc: first byte of the tow cable's record, which follows the three AT-AT records (page 0, P0_9561 on): 0 while no cable is out, bit 3 set by P0_9915 once it has caught a walker's legs. byte 2 is its mode and byte 3 a timer. the AT-AT code tests it before letting the walkers go at the end of the part and before the leg catch test, and clears it when a caught walker blows up

5098.name: s1_tx
5098.desc: MS_TX+M_S1: the player's universe x position, word

50FC.name: cable_tz
50FC.desc: MS_TZ+M_AL: word, the height of the tow cable's end in its unit vector block at M_AL. the cable code moves it and atat_move_all sets it to half the height of a falling walker + $0300 every frame

5006.name: M_AX
5006.desc: CONCAT RESULT (Atari's name in Star Wars): word, A.X of the matrix MS_CNCT leaves. the head aim routines of pages 0 and 1 (P0_8AAC, P1_8A7E) go on only when its high byte is negative

questions: P0:9163 gives a spawned AT-AT the type byte $29 and the demo table at P0:86E7 uses 1 and 9. bit 1 (falling), bit 5 (may shoot, P0:8B68) and bit 7 (gun side) are settled in this range, what bits 0 and 3 mean is not: nothing in $85EC-$8BFF tests them

P0:8AAC the sign test of $5006 after MS_CNCT is read as the head facing the ship (the forward axes of head and ship opposed). the code only shows that the aim is skipped when the high byte is positive

P0:8BB4 object $1A is drawn only when the body was in view this frame and object $19 is drawn last, both from the points of object $18 (objects $18-$1A share one point table). which part of the head each of the three is was not checked against shapes_preview.html
P0:88FB ADDD #$0000 on the x position in the fall mode does nothing, apparently a speed constant left at 0
P0:866E/P0:866F the listing splits the last entry of atat_init_tab in two rows (a label at P0_866F). the table is plain data, 3 entries of 10 bytes from P0_8656 to P0_8673
the leg records labelled at P0:8BEB run on past the end of this stretch to $8C26 (12 records of 5 bytes, $8BEB-$8C26). the last one starting in range is at $8BFF

$5006 is given Atari's Star Wars name M_AX and $5098 the name s1_tx after the existing s1_ty and s1_tz. $4AD2 (cable_rec) and $50FC (cable_tz) belong to the tow cable code at P0_9561-P0_992A, outside this stretch: if that stretch's annotation names them differently, its names should win
